title: Bible Story: Light and the Created World
subtheme: Bible Story: Light and the Created World
description: The opening creation story names light, land, water, and living things. Optional Bible interest: Genesis 1.
cardDescription: The opening creation story names light, land, water, and living things. Optional Bible interest: Genesis 1.
focus: Story setting: Genesis 1. Read the names as part of this particular story, rather than a chapter-and-verse quiz.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Dark time between sunset and dawn
Plant part from which a new plant grows
Tall plant with a woody trunk
Sweet produce such as an apple
Animal with feathers and a beak
Water animal with fins and gills
Bright point in the night sky
Natural satellite seen in Earth's night sky

answerNotes.LIGHT: Brightness making objects visible. This scene follows Genesis 1; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.NIGHT: Night is the dark part of the daily cycle. Dusk is the fading-light period around the approach of night.
answerNotes.SKY: Sky describes the overhead view from the ground. Clouds, the Sun, the Moon, and stars can all appear in that view.
answerNotes.SEED: A seed contains the beginning of a new plant. A seed packet's planting instructions describe how to help it start growing.
answerNotes.TREE: Trees have woody trunks and branches. Familiar garden trees may provide fruit, flowers, or shade, sometimes all three.
answerNotes.FRUIT: Everyday fruit dishes can mix several kinds of plant produce. The serving word is culinary and does not require a botanical classification.
answerNotes.BIRD: Birds have feathers, beaks, and wings. Not every bird flies, so feathers are a more dependable identifying feature than flight alone.
answerNotes.FISH: Fish live in water and breathe through gills. A seal or otter swims too, but it is a mammal rather than a fish.
answerNotes.STAR: A star can mean a distant sun or a pointed decorative shape. Christmas ornaments represent the shape rather than an actual celestial object.
answerNotes.SUN: The Sun is a star. Its closeness makes it look much larger and brighter than the points of light seen at night.
answerNotes.DAY: Twenty-four-hour period. This scene follows Genesis 1; the passage gives the story's context.

answerNotes.GARDEN: A garden is an area cultivated for plants. A single bed or plot can be one part of a larger garden.
answerNotes.TREE: Trees have woody trunks and branches. Familiar garden trees may provide fruit, flowers, or shade, sometimes all three.
answerNotes.FRUIT: Everyday fruit dishes can mix several kinds of plant produce. The serving word is culinary and does not require a botanical classification.
answerNotes.RIVER: A river is flowing water in a channel. In the baptism scene, Jordan is the proper name of the river.
answerNotes.SEED: A seed contains the beginning of a new plant. A seed packet's planting instructions describe how to help it start growing.
answerNotes.LEAF: Leaves use light to help a plant make food. The flat blade and its veins are useful details to notice when identifying a leaf.
answerNotes.NAME: A name identifies a person or thing. In a family album, adding names helps later readers recognize the people pictured.
answerNotes.EDEN: Garden named in the story of Adam and Eve. This scene follows Genesis 2–3; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.ADAM: Eve's companion in the garden of Eden. This scene follows Genesis 2–3; the passage gives the story's context.

answerNotes.ARK: Noah's large boat in Genesis. This scene follows Genesis 6–7; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.WOOD: Wood comes from trees and has a grain. Following that grain when sanding usually leaves a smoother surface.
answerNotes.FAMILY: Family can include several generations and relatives by marriage. A family tree shows relationships rather than everyone's physical appearance.
answerNotes.BIRD: Birds have feathers, beaks, and wings. Not every bird flies, so feathers are a more dependable identifying feature than flight alone.
answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.
answerNotes.RAIN: Rain is liquid water falling from clouds. Snow and hail reach the ground in solid forms instead.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.NOAH: Builder of the Bible's ark. This scene follows Genesis 6–7; the passage gives the story's context.

answerNotes.RAINBOW: Colored arc seen when sun shines through rain. This scene follows Genesis 8–9; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.ARK: In Noah's story, ark names the large boat. Other Bible passages use the same English word for a sacred chest, a different object.
answerNotes.LEAF: Leaves use light to help a plant make food. The flat blade and its veins are useful details to notice when identifying a leaf.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.SKY: Sky describes the overhead view from the ground. Clouds, the Sun, the Moon, and stars can all appear in that view.
answerNotes.CLOUD: Clouds contain tiny water droplets, ice crystals, or both. Their gray appearance does not mean the water itself is gray.
answerNotes.DRY: Dry can be an adjective or an action. It can describe laundry after airing or what happens when moisture leaves a flower bundle.
answerNotes.DOVE: Bird often associated with a soft cooing call. This scene follows Genesis 8–9; the passage gives the story's context.
